task.description:
Investigate GH #594 (ISS-0626, MAJOR): python3 tools/lint_handoffs.py reports 263 BLOCKER + 195 MAJOR + 1 MINOR across 2269 historical handoffs (checked 2026-05-22 through 2026-08-07). This was discovered incidentally during WF03-GH495-20260808's Step Final and filed per CLAUDE.md's No Issue Left Local-Only directive -- it is NOT a new defect class, it is a fresh quantification of the long-standing bookkeeping gap CLAUDE.md's own Bookkeeping Is Not Optional section already documents (2026-08-05 audit: log-append rate 44%->0.4%, registry coverage 3.4%, timestamp validity 8.6%).

Categories per the issue body (docs/issues/ISS-0626.json has the full detail -- read it):
- H001 (11+ files): unparseable JSON -- trailing commas, invalid control characters, one file that fails to decode as UTF-8 at all
- H002 (8 files, all in WF02-iss105-token-model-schema-20260611): 'result' field is a JSON STRING instead of an object -- any h['result']['status'] lookup raises TypeError
- H003 (dozens of files): completed_at precedes started_at -- inverted or local-time-labelled-Z timestamps, corrupting retrospective variance calculations
- H009 (~20 files): a PENDING/IN_PROGRESS step has later COMPLETED steps in the same run -- pipeline advanced past a step it never formally closed
- H010: handoffs/registry.json is missing 82.3% of all historical handoffs from its index

THIS IS A LARGE, MULTI-CATEGORY ISSUE spanning ~3 months of project history. Per CLAUDE.md's batch-cap philosophy (the same principle that led to narrowing GH-495's scope earlier in this loop), do NOT attempt to fix all 2269 handoffs' worth of findings in one WF-03 run. Your job is DIAGNOSIS AND TRIAGE, not blind bulk-fixing:

1. Run `python3 tools/lint_handoffs.py` yourself and capture the full categorized output.
2. For EACH category (H001, H002, H003, H009, H010), determine: is this safely auto-fixable by a mechanical script (e.g. H001's JSON syntax errors, H002's string-vs-object result field, H010's registry reconciliation against the handoffs/ directory tree), or does it require case-by-case judgment (e.g. H003's timestamp inversions -- can you always safely infer the correct timestamp, or would guessing wrong make the audit trail WORSE than leaving it flagged)? For H009 (pipeline advanced past an unclosed step), determine whether the safe fix is to mark the orphaned step COMPLETED retroactively (with what evidence?) or FAILED/ABANDONED, or whether it must be left as a permanent, honest record of an irregularity that already happened and cannot be un-happened.
3. Propose a PHASED remediation plan: which categories can be fixed by a single mechanical script in THIS run (low-risk, high-confidence), and which need to be split into separate follow-up issues for careful case-by-case handling (same pattern as GH-495 -> ISS-0624/ISS-0625). Do not assume everything must be fixed in this one run -- a wrong-guess fix to an audit trail is worse than an honestly-flagged gap.
4. Route to CODE-DESIGNER with this triage and remediation plan -- CODE-DESIGNER will design the actual mechanical-fix script(s) for whichever categories you determine are safe to fix now. Do not implement fixes yourself.
acceptance_criteria: Full categorized lint_handoffs.py output captured and read
Each category (H001/H002/H003/H009/H010) assessed for safe-mechanical-fix vs needs-case-by-case-judgment
Phased remediation plan proposed: what this run fixes now vs. what gets split into follow-up issues
Routed to CODE-DESIGNER with the triage, not implemented directly
No blind bulk-fix that risks corrupting the audit trail further

result.summary:
DIAGNOSIS/TRIAGE COMPLETE (no fixes implemented, per Step 1->Step 2 boundary). Re-ran `python3 tools/lint_handoffs.py` (via .venv/Scripts/python.exe -- python3 is not on PATH in this workspace) against the full corpus: 2270 handoffs checked, 263 BLOCKER + 195 MAJOR + 1 MINOR = 459 findings, broken out by check code: H003 148, H008 88, H007 69, H013 53, H009 38, H004 34, H001 11, H002 9, H005 5, H006 3, H010 1. Read tools/lint_handoffs.py source in full to ground triage in actual check logic (H001-H013, 13 codes total; only 11 appear in current findings -- H011/H012 orchestrator.log checks currently clean). Sample-checked 2-3 real files per category rather than trusting the summary text alone.

TRIAGE VERDICT:
SAFE MECHANICAL FIX (this run's remit, routed to CODE-DESIGNER):
  - H002 (9 files, all WF02-iss105-token-model-schema-20260611): result field is a JSON string; json.loads(result) round-trips cleanly into the exact expected object (verified on step-00-backend-dev-gitsetup.json). Deterministic unwrap, no data invented.
  - H008 (88 files): UTF-8 BOM prefix strip. Pure byte-level operation, content unchanged.
  - H010 (1 finding covering 1868/2270 files): registry.json reconciliation is purely additive -- scan handoffs/ tree, add any handoff_id missing from registry.entries using that handoff's OWN recorded created_at/status/etc, never inventing data. Worst case is a stale/duplicate entry, not a fabricated fact.
  - H006 partial (2 of 3): 'FAILED'->'FAIL' and 'PARTIAL_PASS'->'PARTIAL' are unambiguous synonym-normalizations; safe to fold into the same script. The 3rd value 'CONDITIONAL' has no 1:1 mapping and is excluded.
  - H001 partial (~7 of 11): PowerShell curly-quote/cp1252-encoding corruption (verified: WF02-lua06-16-20260528/step-02-backend-dev.json decodes cleanly as cp1252 and re-parses as valid JSON with identical key structure). Recoverable IF the repair script only accepts a fix when the repaired file re-parses AND a byte-diff shows only the targeted corrupted characters changed (verify-before-write, not blind pattern substitution).

NEEDS CASE-BY-CASE JUDGMENT OR PERMANENT ACKNOWLEDGMENT (split to follow-up issue, NOT this run):
  - H003 (148 BLOCKER): completed_at < started_at, non-whole-hour. No source in the file recovers the true timestamp -- any fix is fabrication.
  - H004 (34 BLOCKER): started_at < created_at. Same unrecoverable-history problem, opposite direction.
  - H013 (53 BLOCKER): whole-hour-offset clock skew (confirmed 3.9-4.0h clustering on samples -- the documented .ToUniversalTime()-omission signature). Offset is computable but the causal timezone is not recorded in the file; correcting it still requires inferring an unrecorded fact.
  - H005 (5 BLOCKER): status COMPLETED but completed_at unset outright. Nothing to recover from.
  - H009 (38 MAJOR): PENDING/IN_PROGRESS step with later COMPLETED siblings in the same run. Marking it COMPLETED/FAILED after the fact fabricates evidence that was never recorded -- this is a real historical process irregularity (exactly the fabrication risk the handoff's own task.description warned about), not a data-entry error.
  - H001 remainder (~4 of 11): genuine structural typos, e.g. handoffs/ADHOC-gh402-db-cleanup-hang-20260803/step-00-backend-dev-db-cleanup.json line 46 closes an object with ']' instead of '}' -- requires understanding which delimiter was intended, i.e. per-file judgment, not a blind pattern.
  - H006 CONDITIONAL (1 of 3): no unambiguous target value; needs the file's own context read by hand, or LEGAL_RESULT_STATUS may need to grow to accept it as a legitimate pre-enum historical state.
  - H007 (69 findings, ~10 distinct files, all WF02-api07-20260523): early alternate schema (workflow_id+sequence instead of run_id+step) -- values are present, just under different key names. Renaming keys on historical record files is a schema-migration decision that needs explicit sign-off, not a silent script alongside H002/H008/H010.

FILED FOLLOW-UP: docs/issues/ISS-0627.json / GitHub #596 (https://github.com/tvolodi/R-Co/issues/596) covers all 8 needs-judgment categories above (292 of 459 findings), added to the global queue via tools/queue_add.py for a future WF-03 run -- same phased-split pattern used for GH-495 -> ISS-0624/ISS-0625. docs/issues/ISS-0626.json's own scope was narrowed in place to cover only the safe-mechanical subset (H002/H008/H010/H006-partial/H001-partial, ~98 of 459 findings) that CODE-DESIGNER designs a repair for next.

Note: an early `queue_add.py --help` probe accidentally wrote a malformed placeholder entry into handoffs/global_queue.json (issue_id '--help', since the script has no flag parser and treats the first arg as a literal issue_id) -- caught and reverted immediately before any commit; queue_add.py has no --help/-h support, first positional arg is always the issue_id.

issues.description: queue_add.py has no --help/-h flag handling; an unrecognized flag-like first argument is silently treated as a literal issue_id and written to the queue. Low risk (caught by review before commit) but worth a follow-up hardening pass: reject args starting with '--' that aren't recognized flags instead of accepting them as issue_id.

result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGNER (WF-03 Step 2) with this triage. Design scope: a single mechanical repair script covering ISS-0626's narrowed remit only -- H002 (unwrap JSON-string result), H008 (strip UTF-8 BOM), H010 (additive registry.json reconciliation from handoffs/ tree), H006 partial (FAILED->FAIL, PARTIAL_PASS->PARTIAL only), and H001 partial (~7 encoding-corruption files, verify-before-write: accept a repair only if the output re-parses as valid JSON AND a byte-diff confirms only the corrupted characters changed). Do NOT design fixes for H003/H004/H005/H009/H013/H007/H006-CONDITIONAL/H001-structural -- those are explicitly out of scope, tracked under ISS-0627/GH-596.
